function: Excluded, system (p. 5): over-the-air (AirComp) gradient aggregation for semi-asynchronous federated learning (area 7) over an OFDM-based SISO link with no RIS: "we consider OFDM-based SISO transmission".
notes: Reason system (code 6), shown on p. 5: "In our model, we consider OFDM-based SISO transmission." Each client's channel is a diagonal matrix of per-subcarrier coefficients with path loss and Rayleigh fading (p. 5), and the simulation has one base station and 100 users with "additive white Gaussian noise (AWGN), path loss, and Rayleigh fading" and no antenna arrays (p. 11). MIMO appears only in related work (p. 2) and RIS only in an author biography (p. 17). Codes 1 to 5 do not apply: it is a research article that proposes and evaluates SA-AirFed; federated learning over the air passes no_learning; the trained model is aggregated over the air, clients "transmit their gradients simultaneously over the same frequency band via AirComp" (p. 5), with AirComp power control solved as sub-problem P2 (p. 9), so the work is area 7 rather than above_phy or another function. Quantitative results exist (Table II on p. 5, Figs. 3 to 8 on pp. 12 to 14), but system is the first code that applies. The PDF is the paper of the DOI: its title and DOI 10.1109/TCOMM.2025.3582727 are on p. 1.
